bull.t: High gross margins and revenue growth
bull.b: Sustained high gross margins (~82%) and positive revenue growth signal durable unit economics for enzyme products and services. Strong margins provide structural capacity to fund R&D and scale manufacturing while absorbing SG&A, supporting long-term margin sustainability if commercial mix holds.

A profitable, established small-molecule segment generates recurring product revenues and real-world validation through 13 branded products. This cash-positive franchise underpins platform investment, reduces reliance on single projects, and strengthens commercial credibility with pharma/CDMO partners.

bull.t: Added liquidity from equity offering and stated cash runway
bull.b: The $23.1M net proceeds from the July 2026 equity offering, combined with management's stated runway to end-2027, meaningfully extend funding for the GMP build and scale-up. This reduces near-term financing pressure and gives time to convert partnerships and operational milestones.

bear.t: Rising leverage and weaker balance sheet
bear.b: Material increase in leverage erodes financial flexibility and elevates refinancing and interest risks. With equity diminished by ongoing losses, higher debt magnifies downside in execution setbacks and constrains strategic options for funding GMP build or absorbing delayed partner payments.

bear.t: Persistent negative operating and free cash flow
bear.b: Ongoing cash burn requires recurring external funding or material margin/profit improvement to attain self-sufficiency. Continued negative operating and free cash flow can force dilutive financings, limit R&D/capex flexibility, and increase vulnerability if partner milestones slip.

A quarter driven by one-time Merck recognition highlights concentration and timing risk. Back-half weighted guidance, ongoing scale-up (100g to 0.5kg) and uncertain partnership conversion mean durable revenue depends on executing technical scale, converting CDMO/pharma talks, and proving repeatable commercial demand.
